Three small sounds, and Fly's loop

Phase 1, D4. Focus start, break start and completion, made in SoundCraft from its built-in synths only, so nothing needs a licence. They'll be heard in libraries and in bed, so they are short, soft and low in the register, and none of them is an alarm. Please listen on your phone's speaker as well as on headphones.

Focus start, break start, then completion, with a pause between each. On an iPhone, if you hear nothing, check the ring switch: the app itself will stay quiet when it is on silent.

Focus start

A focus session starts.

Two soft notes rising a fifth, C5 to G5. The phrase stays open, because the work is ahead.

Fly's ambient loop

Today's file is 1,219 KB, of which 376 KB is empty padding. Re-encoded as mono AAC at 64 kbit/s it is 566 KB. One thing turned up: the recording has never looped cleanly. It opens with 112 ms of silence and a fade-in, and it ends on a hard cut, so every 70 seconds Fly's sound drops out for a moment and clicks. "Hear the loop point" plays the last four seconds and runs on into the start.

Today's file

What ships in v1.3.1, unchanged.

1,219 KB · 96 kbit/s · 70.3 s

Re-encoded, same loop

The file this branch ships. The same sound and the same dropout at the loop point.

566 KB · 64 kbit/s · 70.3 s · the same 3,099,648 samples, no time shift

Re-encoded, seamless loop

A suggestion for you to decide. The first 0.39 s (the silence and the fade-in) are trimmed, and the last 1.51 s fade into the start, so it wraps with no gap. It is 1.9 s shorter.

549 KB · 64 kbit/s · 68.4 s · start and end within 0.11 dB of each other

The app restarts a loop by seeking to the start, which can add a short gap of its own on the phone. These buttons play each file's own join, with nothing added. Sizes are in KB of 1,024 bytes, as the 25 KB budget is.

Please tell me

  1. The three sounds: are they right as they are, or should any be softer, brighter, shorter or a different tune?
  2. Fly's loop: keep today's loop as it is, or use the seamless one?
  3. Does Fly at 64 kbit/s sound the same to you as today's file?

Reply in the chat. Your words go into the D4 record as you write them.

Every figure comes from art/sound/report.json, written by node scripts/sound/build.mjs, which rebuilds each sound from its script in art/sound/; --check compares the rebuild with these files byte for byte. Loudness is the momentary maximum (EBU R 128, a 400 ms window), the fair comparison for sounds this short. Peaks are each sound decoded from the shipped file. Made with soundcraft-cli 0.14.0 and ffmpeg 8.1.1.
